title: Corosolic acid modulates RANKL-triggered signaling to suppress osteoclastogenesis and ovariectomy-induced bone loss.
authors: Zhao, Chuanyong; Wu, Fanghui; Zhao, Liben; Zhong, Jiangtao; Huang, Chenhao; Jiang, Zhangchi; Zheng, Jingqi; Yang, Shengwu; Zhang, Chunwu; Zhang, Lei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究科罗索酸通过结合RANKL抑制破骨细胞分化，虽涉及分子对接但核心是药物-蛋白互作与骨代谢，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合体系，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Osteoporosis is typified by increased bone degradation mediated through osteoclast activity, necessitating innovative interventions. This research explores the therapeutic efficacy of corosolic acid (CA), a triterpenoid recognized for its antioxidative capacity, emphasizing its mechanism through binding to RANKL to inhibit osteoclast development and reinforce redox balance. High-throughput transcriptome sequencing assessed CA's effects on osteoclast gene networks during differentiation. Combined molecular docking and RANKL-induced signaling cascade assessment elucidated CA's molecular regulatory mechanism governing RANKL-activated osteoclastogenesis. CA impeded RANKL-stimulated differentiation of bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMMs) into osteoclasts and disrupted F-actin ring assembly without cytotoxicity. At the molecular level, CA interfered with RANKL-initiated activation of the canonical NF-kappaB and MAPK pathways, evidenced by suppressed phosphorylation of IkappaB-alpha, ERK, JNK, and p38, and concurrent downregulation of osteoclast-specific transcriptional markers. Moreover, CA restricted NFATc1 translocation into the nucleus. In addition to inhibiting osteoclastogenesis, CA modulated oxidative stress by curbing reactive oxygen species (ROS) production and augmenting antioxidant enzyme expression. In vivo, using an ovariectomy-induced bone loss model, CA treatment led to notable improvements in trabecular bone architecture. Collectively, these data highlight CA's potential to mitigate osteoclastic bone resorption through targeted RANKL inhibition, suppressing NF-kappaB/MAPK signaling and redox regulation, underscoring its therapeutic potential for postmenopausal osteoporosis.
abstract_zh: 骨质疏松症以破骨细胞活性介导的骨降解增加为特征，亟需创新性干预措施。本研究探讨了科罗索酸（corosolic acid, CA）——一种以其抗氧化能力著称的三萜类化合物——的治疗功效，重点阐明其通过结合RANKL抑制破骨细胞发育并强化氧化还原平衡的机制。高通量转录组测序评估了CA在分化过程中对破骨细胞基因网络的影响。结合分子对接和RANKL诱导的信号级联评估，阐明了CA调控RANKL激活的破骨细胞生成的分子机制。CA阻断了RANKL刺激的骨髓来源巨噬细胞（BMMs）向破骨细胞的分化，并破坏了F-actin环组装，且无细胞毒性。在分子水平上，CA干扰了RANKL启动的经典NF-kappaB和MAPK通路的激活，表现为IkappaB-alpha、ERK、JNK和p38磷酸化的抑制，以及破骨细胞特异性转录标志物的同步下调。此外，CA限制了NFATc1向核内的转位。除抑制破骨细胞生成外，CA还通过抑制活性氧（ROS）产生和增强抗氧化酶表达来调节氧化应激。在体内，使用卵巢切除诱导的骨丢失模型，CA治疗导致小梁骨结构的显著改善。综合来看，这些数据突显了CA通过靶向RANKL抑制、抑制NF-kappaB/MAPK信号通路及氧化还原调节来减轻破骨细胞骨吸收的潜力，强调了其对绝经后骨质疏松症的治疗前景。
